rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate keeps the safe passes and pushes obfuscation up moderately while respecting that flops-2 is a tight floating-point loop where runtime overhead is the dominant risk: SUB is emphasized first (cheap, high security/diversity on arithmetic-heavy code, minimal correctness risk), SPLIT is kept high since it adds control-flow diversity at near-zero cost and helps break up the single large main for the other passes, and BCF is raised to a moderate level to add opaque predicates but capped by an elevated RuntimeCost weight so the hot FP loop is not smothered; IBR and IGV sit at mid weights to add indirect branching/global indirection diversity without compounding dispatch overhead. FLA and ICALL are omitted entirely: with only one substantial function, flattening converts a clean numeric loop into a dispatcher-dominated state machine whose runtime penalty on a flops benchmark is severe while its added reverse-engineering value over BCF+SPLIT is marginal, and indirect-call transformation has almost no call sites to work with here, so it would add risk and size for negligible diversity.
